newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Albright proposes new NATO, Russia talks.
newsitem.headline: Albright proposes new NATO, Russia talks.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright, seeking to lessen Moscow's opposition to NATO enlargement, proposed on Tuesday that the alliance and Russia develop a joint military brigade.

In a speech to NATO foreign ministers aimed at solidifying the alliance's position on expansion and assuring Russia of NATO's non-threatening intentions, she also proposed a NATO-Russia meeting with potential new alliance members ahead of a summit set for July.

Making the case for a new partnership between NATO and Russia -- which fiercely opposes alliance expansion eastward -- Albright said Russian and NATO planners would "work together at our major military commands."
"And we could begin immediately to develop a joint NATO- Russia brigade," she said.

This would complement NATO's vision of a joint NATO-Russia council "that would promote a regular dialogue on majority security issues, reach concerted decisions whenever possible, and seize opportunities for joint action," she said, in her first speech to NATO since her appointment as America's top diplomat.

The United States has rejected a French proposal for a mini- summit involving the United States, Germany, France, Britain and Russia ahead of the July NATO summit in Madrid that is designed to take decisions on new members.
Albright noted that the alliance has already conducted intensified dialogues with potential NATO members and said this has been "vital" to the process.

But she said: "We need to conduct another round (of talks) at 16-plus-1 this spring to give every ally a chance for direct discussion with potential members and to give every aspirant a fair hearing."
Sixteen-plus-one is the designation given to meetings between the 16 NATO members and Russia, an informal structure that has evolved since the end of the Cold War.
"These dialogues must continue in some form beyond Madrid. We cannot make specific commitments but we can and should offer some programme to bring our partners up to NATO standards," she said.

This gesture is an apparent effort to "cushion" the blow to former Warsaw Pact states which are not invited to join NATO at the Madrid summit by ensuring that the alliance will continue to consider additional future new members.
Albright also proposed that all members of NATO's partnership for peace programme -- which includes Russia and most former Warsaw Pact countries -- should be invited to the July summit in Madrid.
"The alliance must be united and I believe we are united in our policy towards Russia. We cannot realise our shared vision of a united, secure and democratic Europe without Russia," she said.
